Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 1 12, English)
Ashaeiynn Pathshala: Kriya, the Aatma Tattva, and the 70/18/12 Destiny Br eakdown — Tantrik Binding, What Powers True Prosperity , and Why Malefic Grahas Invite Attack

This session's sour ce material arrived as several consecutive pieces with no fr esh opening gr eeting, sankalp, or "welcome to X" framing between them, and the very first piece begins mid-explanation (the r ecor ding's own opening and the devotee question that pr ompted it wer e not captur ed). Because of this, and because the later pieces explicitly r econnect to this session's own kriya/tantrik material (the destiny-per centage teaching dir ectly explains why bad planetary periods invite tantrik attack, tying back to Parts A-F), all of it is tr eated as a single continuous session rather than split into separate sessions. Parts A-F cover kriya (tantrik binding), kriya-cutting, and maran kriya. Parts G-K cover a r elated but br oader teaching that followed dir ectly afterwar d: the aatma tattva/"pr osperity DNA" behind spiritual awakening, the per centage br eakdown of what actually shapes a person's destiny , why bad Shani/Rahu/Ketu periods cr eate the conditions for tantrik attack, a case of a dosha (affliction) invisible in a standar d birth chart, and the signs of genuine deva shakti versus the speaker's own testimony of surviving a r eal tantrik attack. All of this — the kriya material and the destiny/deva-shakti material alike — is pr esented strictly as this teaching's own descriptive, pr otective, and devotional knowledge for existing devotees, never as instructions for performing any such practice on anyone, and never as a substitute for a qualified guru's dir ect guidance. See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document for how this material must be handled.
Part A — What "Kriya" Is, and the Pr econdition of Having Ever Taken God's Name

1. The starting point of a kriya — taking something fr om the target's body or belongings: Per this teaching, a tantrik seeking to perform a "kriya" (a binding ritual connection) begins by taking some small physical item connected to the tar get — illustrated here with soil from near someone's feet, or a piece of their clothing.

2. A necessary pr econdition — the target must have taken God's name at least once in their life: Per this teaching, this kind of tantrik binding can only be performed on a person who has, at some point in their life, taken God's name (even in passing or by accident) — because it is this act that establishes an active astral/subtle body for the ritual to connect to. Per this teaching, a person who has genuinely never invoked God's name at all cannot be reached this way , since the ritual becomes "null and void" and their astral body simply does not function as a tar get for it.

3. What happens when this pr econdition isn't met: Per this teaching, in such cases (where the intended tar get has no active astral connection to work with), practitioners resort to a dif ferent method entirely , described later in this document (Part E).
Part B — How a Tantrik Builds a "Major/Minor" Energy Imbalance to Contr ol Someone

1. The basic method — energizing the taken item far beyond the target's own body: Per this teaching (illustrated with a devotee example referred to here as "Shilpi," whose pallu/garment-end is taken as the item), the practitioner takes the small
item and deliberately channels far more ener gy into it than exists in the tar get's own body — illustratively , ten times as much ener gy to begin with.

2. Why a small amount of extra energy makes no r eal differ ence: Per this teaching, if the tar get's own body already carries very strong, active spiritual ener gy (illustrated as "100% jagriti"), then ener gizing a taken item to only a small fraction of that (illustrated as 1%) has no meaningful ef fect on the tar get at all.

3. The "major/minor" r eversal, once enough energy is added: Per this teaching, if the practitioner instead channels dramatically more ener gy into the taken item (illustrated as multiplying it to 10,000 or even 1,000,000 times its original level), a reversal occurs: the taken item becomes the "major" part of the connected pair , and the tar get's own actual body becomes the comparatively "minor" part — meaning actions performed on the item are now felt throughout the tar get's body .

4. "Jagaran" (awakening) and forming the item into a doll/effigy: Per this teaching, the most important part of this process is the "jagaran" (awakening/activation) of the ener gized item, after which it may be shaped into a doll or ef figy — once this awakened item is made dramatically more "jagrit" (ener gized) than the tar get's own body , it becomes the major part of the connection, and even light contact with the ef figy (for example, a needle) is felt by the tar get.

5. Naming this bond — "kriya": Per this teaching, the ongoing bond/connection between the tar get and the ener gized item is what is specifically called "kriya" — describing the practitioner's ongoing connection to the tar get's body through that item.
Part C — Cutting Kriya Safely: Why Leaving 20% Connected Is Safer Than a Full Cut

1. Why an outright, complete cut is risky: Per this teaching, if a protector (such as someone at Ashaeiynn) severs a kriya bond completely , the originating tantrik will immediately sense it — because a mantra sent by the tantrik functions like something thrown that is expected to land and stay; if the connection is fully severed, the mantra ef fectively "rebounds" back to the tantrik, instantly revealing that the bond has been cut.

2. What happens once a full cut is detected — r epeated r e-binding: Per this teaching, once a tantrik realizes a kriya has been cut, they can simply perform the kriya again (and, if provoked, with even more intensity each time) — describing a potentially endless cycle of binding and re-binding, sometimes continuing for years, and noted as deliberately intended to keep the victim's own mental and emotional ener gy consumed and depleted, which is described as one of the tantrik's core underlying goals independent of any other specific harm.

3. Ashaeiynn's actual appr oach — leaving r oughly 20% of the connection intact: Per this teaching, rather than fully severing a kriya, the safer approach deliberately leaves about 20% of the original connection in place, cutting the remaining roughly 80% — this way , the originating tantrik still perceives an active connection and continues sending ener gy toward the tar get, unaware that only a small fraction of it now has any ef fect.

4. Why this r equires simultaneously gr owing the target's own energy: Per this teaching, for this partial-cut approach to work safely long-term, the tar get's own mantra shakti must be built up dramatically — to twenty or thirty times its own prior level — so that even though a nominal 20% connection remains, the tar get's own body has by then become the "major" part of the relationship and the tantrik's remaining influence becomes negligible in practice.

5. Why the target should not perform a dedicated "kriya-cutting" hawan: Per this teaching, performing a specifically-labeled kriya-cutting ritual/hawan risks alerting the tantrik to what has happened, prompting them to react and restart the binding-andcutting cycle; the recommended approach instead is simply to keep multiplying one's own mantra shakti quietly , without drawing the tantrik's attention to the fact that a cut occurred.

6. The eventual endpoint — locating and neutralizing "r eceptors": Per this teaching, after potentially many cycles of binding and cutting over an extended period, it eventually becomes possible to trace and neutralize the underlying "receptors"

(described here as devta-level entities the tantrik draws on) directly — though this teaching notes this step has both benefits and drawbacks, since among its ef fects is the removal of what is described as a person's own subtle "location" marker , which is not without cost.
Part D — How Tantriks Operate on Multiple People at Once

1. Pre-charging objects for many targets simultaneously: Per this teaching, a practitioner working against many people at once does not rely on personally remembering each tar get individually — instead, physical items connected to each tar get are kept in a fixed location (for example, beneath or near the practitioner's own seat/aasan), and simply touching that location after completing japa reactivates the connection to every tar get simultaneously .

2. A brief, anonymized illustrative case: Per this teaching, one such case (referenced only briefly and without identifying detail here) described a woman troubled by episodes at consistent times of day over roughly two years, tracing to this same "touch and reactivate" pattern on the tantrik's side.
Part E — Sending an External Entity ("Pr et") to Someone Who Has Never Taken God's Name

1. Why a differ ent method is needed for this case: Per this teaching, when a tar get has genuinely never invoked God's name and so has no active astral connection to bind through kriya, a practitioner instead sends an external entity (a "pret"/spirit, colloquially bhoot-pret) directly into the tar get's body .

2. How the entity is pr epar ed and dispatched: Per this teaching, the entity is ener gized/char ged by the practitioner and instructed to enter and settle within the tar get's body; whatever ener gy is subsequently sent by the practitioner is then felt by the target through this entity's presence, typically as pressure, fear , or distress.

3. The intended effect — driving the target toward devotion out of fear: Per this teaching, the resulting fear and pressure are intended to push the tar get toward seeking refuge in God/religious practice — and once the tar get begins doing so, the resident entity itself becomes "char ged" by that devotional activity as well.

4. A "use and thr ow" system — why the entity is never recalled: Per this teaching, once dispatched this way , such an entity is not called back by the practitioner who sent it — described as a "use and throw" system; the entity , left with nowhere else to go, remains lodged in the tar get's body indefinitely .

5. Why intensified devotional practice can sometimes worsen physical discomfort: Per this teaching, this dynamic is of fered as one explanation for why some devoted, elderly practitioners doing intensive puja experience worsening bodily pain as their devotion increases — because a previously dormant, already-resident negative influence becomes activated and agitated by that same intensifying devotional ener gy .
Part F — Maran Kriya (the Death Ritual) and Why It Is Rar ely Practiced
1. What maran kriya is, per this teaching: Per this teaching, maran kriya is described as a ritual capable of causing a tar get's death within roughly four days.

2. Why it is said that "no one truly takes a life" thr ough this practice: Per this teaching, an entity does not simply "end" a life without consequence to the practitioner who directed it; per this teaching, performing this act creates a lasting spiritual debt (dosha) and an ongoing bond between the practitioner and the deceased's own subtle body/being.

3. The consequence — the deceased's subtle being follows the practitioner seeking dir ection: Per this teaching, after the death, the involved subtle being (typically described as operating at a devta-adjacent level) returns to the practitioner , effectively asking what it should do or where it should go next, since the practitioner elevated or "awakened" it to that role — creating an ongoing, dif ficult-to-resolve obligation for the practitioner .

4. Why maran kriya is said to be practiced almost exclusively by those with nothing to lose: Per this teaching, because of this lasting consequence, maran kriya is described as practiced almost exclusively by ascetic or renunciate individuals with no household, family , or property at stake — practitioners with families and possessions are said to avoid it, since the resulting consequences would fall on those attachments; a person with nothing left to lose has comparatively little the consequence can threaten.

5. What happens to an unr esolved entity with no further outlet: Per this teaching, an entity left without any further task or connection may seek out and attach itself to a new person to create a fresh bond (illustrated with the possibility of such an entity tar geting and attaching to an unconnected young woman), perpetuating a similar cycle of attachment and consequence described earlier in this document.
Part G — The Aatma Tattva ("Pr osperity DNA"): One Underlying Awakening, Many Names and Many Paths

1. Many names for one underlying tattva: Per this teaching, the same inner element that dif ferent traditions describe under dif ferent names — aatma tattva (self-element), praan tattva (life-force element), devta tattva (deity element), mada tattva, shakti tattva, or in a more modern phrase, "prosperity DNA" — is one and the same thing, addressed dif ferently depending on the path a practitioner follows; its function is described as making a person a "life magnet" whose attraction/prosperity power grows once it is awakened.

2. Dhyana-marg (the meditation path) calls it "aatma tattva jagriti": Per this teaching, a meditator who controls the senses and pushes awareness out of the body , opening the kundalini shakti's portals as it rises, and eventually reaches what this teaching calls the "kapaat" (a crown-level portal), regards that arrival itself as the ultimate truth — "I am God now ."

3. Guru-marg and the Nath sampradaya call the same event "Shiv-Shakti milan": Per this teaching, practitioners of the guru-centered path, including the Nath sampradaya, describe this identical event at the kapaat as the union ("milan") of Shiv and Shakti, at which point the universe's ener gies begin to be drawn toward the practitioner .

4. Bhakti-marg (the devotional path) r eaches it thr ough dir ect vision of the Lord: Per this teaching, devotees who consider a direct vision/realization ("sakshatkar") of God to be their own tattva and surrender find that once this sakshatkar occurs, their "prosperity DNA" (by whatever name) awakens automatically .

5. The "many r oads to Ashaeiynn" analogy: Per this teaching, just as a person may reach Ashaeiynn by flight, by bus, or on foot — arriving at the same final destination but via very dif ferent experiences en route (one arrives fit, another queasy from the drive, another exhausted from walking) — the same underlying tattva can be awakened by many dif ferent paths and methods; all serious saints/practitioners are described as being in agreement on this point, which is why it is so widely discussed under so many dif ferent names.

6. The common mistake — pulling the tattva "up" without first awakening it: Per this teaching, most people focus only on drawing this tattva up to the kapaat and stop there, for getting that a long path still remains beyond that point; someone who reaches the kapaat without having actually awakened/expanded the tattva along the way risks falling back down afterward.

7. Where the tattva actually r esides — the heart, as a small continuous flame: Per this teaching, scripture states (and this teaching af firms) that a person's aatma tattva resides in the heart, existing as a small, continuously active flame or lamp (diya); when it exits the body , the person's life ends — which is also why it is sometimes called the praan tattva (life-force element).

8. Chakras ar e only a "stair case," not the tattva itself: Per this teaching, chakras are merely an instrument/channel through which this tattva's ener gy can be moved and upgraded — a staircase that leads both upward and toward lower realms — not the source of the tattva's power itself; the speaker states he has personally observed vast numbers of chakras across many dimensions and no longer attaches special importance to any single one of them.

9. The multiverse mechanism behind why pr osperity manifests differ ently for different people: Per this teaching, when the tattva reaches the kapaat, it draws only from whatever "authority"/standing a person's own subtle bodies (sookshm sharirs) have independently earned across their own past lives in the astral/parallel-universe realm — never anyone else's outcomes; this is why two people who awaken the same tattva to the same degree can end up prosperous in completely dif ferent domains (for example, one in cosmetics, another in advertising) — each pulling only what their own parallel-universe subtle bodies had already earned in that specific domain.

10. The Gita cr oss-r eference — you r eceive only your own karma's fruit: Per this teaching, this mechanism is of fered as an explanation for why Bhagwan Krishna teaches in the Gita that a person receives fruit strictly according to their own karma and nothing else — every dimension's karma is included in that reckoning, not just the present life's.

1 1. Krishna's "laddu manifestation" illustration of the same multiverse for ce: Per this teaching, when Bhagwan Krishna manifested a laddu, his subtle body would go and place a laddu in each of many parallel universes (illustratively , 99 out of 100); the resulting "force tendency" from that near -universal presence then caused the laddu to spontaneously appear in the remaining, final universe as well — illustrating that even Krishna's apparent miracles rested on real ef fort across many dimensions, not ef fortless magic; this mastery over his own aatma tattva to an "extreme level" (traditionally described as his 16 kalas) is why he is called Parmatma (the supreme/complete atma).

12. The Ida-Pingala-vayu technical mechanism of awakening: Per this teaching, japa (repeated chanting, e.g. "Jai Shri Ram") produces a particular vayu (subtle breath/air current); as this vayu balances the Ida and Pingala nadis, the sushumna is awakened, and the udaan vayu carries the awakening upward — this vayu functions like the spark needed to start a generator (requiring a potential dif ference between two terminals), and that "spark" is what ignites and grows a person's praan shakti with each repetition.

13. Why r epetition matters — the spark must be struck again and again: Per this teaching, each act of heartfelt prayer/japa restrikes this spark, and doing so many times a day (illustratively , a thousand times) causes the praan tattva to keep growing rather than depleting, in turn increasing its "grahan shakti" (holding/receiving capacity) — the very thing that determines how effectively future prayers will work.

14. Why a borr owed, one-time jolt of energy fr om someone else doesn't last: Per this teaching, if the practice's own ener gy is not present, a chakra "awakened" temporarily from an outside source (for example, briefly ener gized by the speaker himself) behaves like a generator run below its rated load — it works only for a moment and shuts of f again once that outside support is withdrawn, precisely because the practitioner's own sustained vayu/japa was not present to keep it running.

15. The risk of falling after real awakening — why fast r esults ar en't promised: Per this teaching, even great, accomplished saints/mahatmas have been known to fall back into "maya" after reaching a genuinely awakened state, if lured by money or other desires, wasting a lifetime's earned praan shakti — which is why this teaching deliberately avoids promising fast, effortless results and instead emphasizes sustained, unglamorous daily practice.
Part H — The Destiny Per centage Br eakdown: Kundalini Shakti, Tapobal, and Why Astrology "W orks"

1. The overall per centage br eakdown of what shapes a person's destiny: Per this teaching, a person's total destiny is described, illustratively , as: roughly 70% governed by their own kundalini shakti's potential ef fect; roughly 18% governed by this-life tapobal (accumulated spiritual practice/merit); and the remaining roughly 12% tied to karma bound up with prarabdha
(already-written destiny) — itself split into about 9% for physical ef fort/hard work and about 3% that is the only portion genuinely "free" for a person's own independent will.

2. Why the 70% (kundalini shakti) and 18% (this-life tapobal) portions ar e effectively zer o for most people: Per this teaching, since almost no one has actually awakened their kundalini shakti, that 70% portion becomes "null and void" for them in practice; likewise, simple daily worship alone (lighting a lamp, incense, reciting a chalisa) is said to take some 20-25 years of consistent, negativity-free practice before it yields real siddhi, so for most people this 18% portion is also not yet active — leaving roughly 88% of the theoretical breakdown ef fectively at zero.

3. The remaining 12%, and why the "3%" is wher e astr ology actually operates: Per this teaching, of the last 12%, about 9% is bound up with rigid, unchangeable prarabdha-linked factors (family profession, parents' traits and habits, physical build, mother tongue, neighbors, genetics) that cannot be altered no matter the ef fort — illustrated with a father who writes lefthanded whose child, however trained, will still feel drawn to the left hand; only the remaining roughly 3% is a domain a person can genuinely act on for themselves, and this small, low-ef fort domain (a specific color , a specific day , a specific ritual object) is exactly the domain that astrology and small remedial rituals claim to influence.

4. Why astr ology appears so r eliably accurate for most people: Per this teaching, because the 70% and 18% portions are effectively inactive for the overwhelming majority of people, virtually all of the ef fective influence on their lives is concentrated in this small remaining domain that the navagraha (nine planets) govern — which is why astrology can appear correct 70-80% of the time or more for most people, and why astrologers who read a person's birth-chart accurately can predict outcomes and dates with real precision within that domain, even though its actual overall share of destiny is small.

5. A person with an awakened kundalini shakti is largely outside astr ology's r each: Per this teaching, once a person's kundalini shakti is genuinely awakened, their own character and choices ("sankalp," a deliberate intention/vow) can redirect what would otherwise be planetary influence, ef fectively bringing it within their own 3% domain instead — meaning astrology becomes far less predictive for such a person, since a determined, awakened sankalp accomplishes what is willed, on its own timeline, regardless of what the birth chart shows.
Part I — Why Bad Shani/Rahu/Ketu Periods Invite Tantrik Kriya, and Why Daily (Not Lump-Sum) Practice Is Required

1. How the navagraha draw their shar e of a person's daily praan shakti: Per this teaching, each of the nine grahas claims its own agreed percentage of a person's daily praan shakti (life-force ener gy) for a fixed period (a "dasha," ranging from roughly one to thirty years); during that period the graha only takes from the person's ener gy and does not give back, which is why sustained bad periods can visibly drain a person (for example, causing hair to thin or gray prematurely — a pattern this teaching notes af fects both men and women, contrary to the common assumption that it is mainly a male experience).

2. Which grahas' bad periods specifically cr eate the conditions for tantrik kriya: Per this teaching, when a person's Shani (Saturn), Rahu, and/or Ketu are af flicted or in a dif ficult dasha, this creates the specific conditions under which a tantrik attack ("kriya," as described in Parts A-F of this document) becomes more likely to succeed — an important direct link between this teaching's destiny-percentage framework and its earlier teaching on tantrik binding.

3. Why a bad graha period leaves lingering negativity even after it "ends": Per this teaching, when a malefic graha's dasha period concludes, it is expected to give back what it took, but because the graha never resolved the negativity or unaddressed ancestral (pitru) matters it deposited along with taking, that residual negativity can remain lodged in the body even after the graha's period has technically ended — leaving some people receiving only a small fraction of destined good fortune (illustrated as "only five" out of an expected much lar ger sum) because negativity absorbs the rest before it can manifest.

4. Why the malefic graha's r emaining energy demand must be met daily , not in one lump sum: Per this teaching, a malefic graha's dasha requires a fixed amount of ener gy from the person every single day for the full duration of its period; a person who instead sits for a lar ge, one-time japa session cannot "pre-pay" for future days — illustrated with the analogy of taking a whole month's worth of vitamins in a single dose, which does not prevent needing more the very next day — so consistent daily practice (for example, two hours of japa every day) throughout the dasha's duration is what is actually required to neutralize its draw .

5. Guru-sannidhya can make even a genuinely bad dasha painless: Per this teaching, a person under sustained guru-sannidhya (the guru's presence/care) can pass through even a dif ficult graha dasha (such as sade-sati) with little or no visible hardship, because the guru's own sankalp channels the graha's due ener gy on the devotee's behalf — described in this teaching as one of the direct, tangible benefits of guru-sannidhya.

6. The warning against trying to be "your own her o": Per this teaching, a devotee facing a dif ficult dasha should not attempt to personally negotiate with or manage the af fected graha alone ("don't try to be your own hero"); the recommended approach is to surrender the matter to the guru/devta through prayer rather than attempting an independent, self-directed remedy .
Part J — Beyond the Birth Chart: A Curse Invisible to Standard Astrology , and a Case of Guru Chandal Yog

1. The blind spot in standard, birth-chart-only astr ology: Per this teaching, conventional astrologers build a person's chart entirely from their exact birth data and can predict outcomes and dates with real accuracy within that framework — but this method has a structural blind spot: it cannot account for another person's independent free will, spiritual transformation, or curse, since none of that was written into the original chart at the moment of birth.

2. The "Dhawal" illustration — an unwritten dosha cr eated by someone else's independent tapasya: Per this teaching (illustrated with a devotee example referred to as "Dhawal," details kept general here per this teaching's own privacy practice), a person once mocked or insulted Dhawal without knowing that Dhawal had, independently , undertaken serious spiritual practice and inner transformation; the resulting anger/agni within Dhawal produced a "shaap" (curse) tattva that settled onto the person who had insulted him as a dosha (af fliction) — one that does not appear anywhere in that person's own birth chart, because it originated from someone else's independent spiritual action rather than from the person's own birth-time planetary configuration.

3. Why such a dosha can persist acr oss generations, or disappear entirely: Per this teaching, a dosha created this way can potentially show up in the birth charts of the af fected person's own children later on; however , if the af fected person undertakes suf ficiently high-level sadhna themselves, the dosha can be purified away so completely that it never shows up in any chart at all.

4. Why r esolving this kind of dosha r equires a guru or gifted seer , not a standard astr ologer: Per this teaching, because this class of dosha has no birth-chart signature, identifying and resolving it requires a guru or someone with genuine inner sight who can perceive its true origin directly , rather than someone relying purely on conventional birth-chart analysis.

5. A related teaching point — one person's spiritual transformation changes many linked people's destinies at once: Per this teaching, when a person undertakes serious spiritual transformation, it does not change only their own fate — it changes the fate of everyone whose own destiny is linked to theirs (illustrated as potentially "lakhs" of people); this is of fered as part of the explanation for why deep transformation often takes longer than a person expects, since so many linked outcomes are being adjusted at once, not just the practitioner's own.

6. The "Neha" anecdote — an esoteric diagnosis beyond conventional astr ology: Per this teaching (illustrated with a devotee referred to as "Neha," a "younger sister" of the speaker whose husband practices astrology; details kept general here per this teaching's own privacy practice), when Neha stayed at Ashaeiynn for a few months, the speaker told her — based on his guru's own guidance rather than conventional chart-reading — that her chart showed signs of a "Guru Chandal Yog" (a specific

inauspicious planetary combination); her husband initially reacted with strong skepticism, but the speaker maintained confidence in the diagnosis (of fering to have it checked point by point against the yog's known symptoms) while Neha herself continued and completed her own sadhna despite the friction.
Part K — The Signs of Genuine Deva Shakti, and the Speaker's Own Testimony of Surviving Tantrik Attack

1. What genuine deva/guru-sannidhya shakti does NOT feel like: Per this teaching, ener gy genuinely received through gurusannidhya never produces a jolt or jerk ("jhatka") to the body , never causes extreme pain, is never accompanied by any sense of negativity , and never produces fear .

2. What genuine deva/guru-sannidhya shakti DOES feel like — the pr ogr ession of signs: Per this teaching, the signs of genuinely received shakti, in the order they are typically first noticed, are: a heaviness at the top of the head (illustratively linked to Hanuman ji's own powerful tattva); a vibration; goosebumps ("rom-rom khade ho jaana") and a tingling/current sensation; a cooling sensation (felt as coolness even in summer heat, like ice placed at a specific point on the back, hands, or head); and, at a more advanced/extreme level, a sensation of water droplets falling on the skin even though nothing is visibly wet and no rain or water is actually present.

3. Why a "jhatka" (jolt) during energy practice is not a sign of anything wr ong with the underlying shakti: Per this teaching, practitioners who experience jolts during their own ener gy practice (including some who worship Devi, Bhagwan Shiva, or Shani Dev) are not experiencing an impure or defective tattva — they simply have not yet learned a specific technique for receiving the ener gy smoothly; the speaker notes that he and other siddha devotees used to experience these jolts themselves, until his own guru taught a specific remedy ("upaay") after which they stopped.

4. The speaker's own testimony — surviving tantrik attack early in his sadhna: Per this teaching, the speaker recounts that early in his own sadhna he came under sustained tantrik attack, before his guru "opened his sight" (drishti) to reveal what was happening; the attacking tantriks were described as powerful enough to describe details of his own breathing and actions from a distance, which frightened him deeply precisely because the threat was invisible and could not be explained to anyone else.

5. How the speaker describes his guru's pr otection manifesting during that period: Per this teaching, the speaker describes his guru's grace during that time as round-the-clock protective sensations — a continuous feeling of water droplets falling on him (even while indoors, including in a bathroom) and an ice-like coolness at various points on his body — along with direct reassurance whenever he called out in fear ("beta, dekh, main yahin hoon" — "child, look, I am right here").

6. How this testimony must be understood, per this teaching's own framing: This account is presented in this teaching strictly as personal, devotional testimony about what guru-sannidhya protection felt like during a real historical attack on the speaker himself — not as a technique, a how-to guide, or advice for a listener to attempt either performing or independently defending against such an attack on their own.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

"Kriya" is a tantrik binding technique that requires the tar get to have taken God's name at least once in their life (otherwise the ritual is null and void); a practitioner takes a small item connected to the tar get, ener gizes it far beyond the tar get's own body's ener gy level, and this "major/minor" imbalance is what allows actions on the item to af fect the tar get. Fully severing a kriya bond alerts the originating tantrik immediately (via a "rebound" ef fect) and typically restarts an endless binding-and-cutting cycle; Ashaeiynn's own approach instead leaves roughly 20% of the connection intact while dramatically growing the tar get's own mantra shakti, so the tantrik believes the bond is still active while it has no real remaining ef fect — and a dedicated, publicly visible "kriya-cutting" ritual is avoided for the same reason.
